IOHN.|223}}</noinclude>maister in Israel, and art thou ignorant of these things? {{verse|chapter=3|verse=11}}† Amen, Amen I say to thee, that we speake that vvhich vve knovv, and that vvhich vve haue seen vve testifie, and our testimonie you receiue not. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=12}}† If I haue spoken to you earthly things, and you beleeue not: hovv if I shal speake to you heauenly things, vvil you beleeue? {{verse|chapter=3|verse=13}}† And no man hath ascended into heauen, but he that descended from heauen, the Sonne of man vvhich is in heauen. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=14}}† And as {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Nu. 21, 9.''}}* Moyses exalted the serpent in the desert, so must the Sonne of man be exalted: {{verse|chapter=3|verse=15}}† that euery one vvhich beleeueth in him, perish not, but may haue life euerlasting. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=16}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō Munday in the whitsonweeke.}}For so God loued the vvorld, that he gaue his only-begotten sonne: that euery one that beleeueth in him, perish not, but may haue life euerlasting.⊣ {{verse|chapter=3|verse=17}}† For God sent not his sonne into the vvorld, to iudge the vvorld, but that the vvorld may be saued by him. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=18}}† He that beleeueth in him, is not iudged. but he that doeth not beleeue, {{sup|‖}} is already iudged: because he hath not beleeued in the name of the only-begotten sonne of God. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=19}}† And this is the iudgment: because the light is come into the vvorld, and men haue loued the darkenesse rather then the light: for their vvorkes vvere euil. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=20}}† For euery one that doeth il, hateth the light, and commeth not to the light, that his vvorkes may not be controuled. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=21}}† But he that doeth veritie, commeth to the light, that his vvorkes may be made manifest, because they vvere done in God.⊣

{{verse|chapter=3|verse=22}}† After these things {{sc|Iesvs}} came and his Disciples into the countrie of Ievvrie: and there he abode vvith them, and baptized. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=23}}† And Iohn also vvas baptizing in Aenon beside Salim: because there vvas much vvater there, and they came, and vvere baptized. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=24}}† For Iohn vvas not yet cast into prison. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=25}}† And there rose a question of Iohns disciples vvith the Ievves concerning purification. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=26}}† And they came to Iohn, and said to him, Rabbi, he that vvas vvith thee beyond Iordan, to vvhom {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 1, 19.''}}* thou didst giue testimonie, behold he baptizeth, and al come to him. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=27}}† Iohn ansvvered and said, A man can not receiue any thing, vnlesse it be giuen him from heauen. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=28}}† Your selues doe beare me vvitnesse, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 1, 20.''}}* that I said, I am not {{sc|Christ}}: but that I am sent before him. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=29}}† He that hath the bride, is the bridegrome: but the frende of the bridegrome that standeth and heareth him, reioyceth vvith ioy for the voice of the bridegrome. This my ioy therfore is {{hws|fil|filled.}}<noinclude>{{rh|||led.}}</noinclude>
